answer: In an agent market for nectar, timber, and juniper, each seller identity must lock a 100-credit bond to receive a fixed order quota. Signed sales enter a public log; two conflicting promises of exclusive ownership of the same numbered lot trigger bond forfeiture. Aliases cannot multiply capacity for free: operating 1,000 sellers requires locking 100,000 credits, and each proven double sale destroys the offending identity’s collateral.
